title: E0076: Information disclosure
plain_english: Leaving `phpinfo()` in committed production code exposes detailed PHP configuration, version, extensions, and environment variables to anyone who can access that page.
why_matters: Attackers can use `phpinfo()` output to: - Fingerprint the server (PHP version, loaded extensions) - Identify version-specific vulnerabilities - Read environment variables and configuration values - Plan targeted attacks against the infrastructure
good_example:
// Remove phpinfo() entirely from production code.
// Use it only in local development and do not commit it.
what_it_checks: `phpinfo()` function calls anywhere in committed source code
